newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals calm, baht awaits data.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals calm, baht awaits data.

text.p: The Thai baht was steady on Thursday ahead of the release of central bank monthly economic data expected later in the session, dealers said.
Sentiment was cautious as the market waits to see the extent to which Thailand's foreign reserve declined after central bank intervention to defend the baht from speculation last month.
The Bank of Thailand will announce April and May economic data at 0800 GMT.
Traders said a sharp fall in reserves would put downward pressure on the baht.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yonchaiyudh has said he does not want to devalue the currency.
The baht was quoted at 25.840/870 at 0430 GMT to the dollar against 25.820/850 late on Wednesday.
But trade was relatively quiet in the onshore market, with comments from former Thai Prime Minister Chatichai Choonhavan in New Delhi having little affect on activity, dealers said.

Chatichai said the Bank of Thailand estimates that gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 5.9 percent in 1997, down from 6.4 percent last year. He also said the government would strongly defend the value of the baht.
The Bank of Thailand kept the baht/dollar midrate unchanged at 25.77. Offshore, the baht was barely changed at 25.400/500 against 25.300/25.400 on Wednesday.
The Malaysian ringgit recovered as dollar gains were capped on the topside near the level where dealers felt the central bank would intervene at 2.5240.
The dollar was well bid in the offshore market but failed to trek beyond 2.5250, which continues to keep ringgit defensive.
"People are still trying to buy the dollar/Malay. There is commericial demand for the dollar before June 30, but market is still long dollars offshore," a European brokerage dealer said.
He said dollar demand was prompted by mid-year book closing and some window-dressing activities.
At 0430 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5200/100, up from 2.5232/42 at its close in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
Malaysian dealers said there was also some caution as the system could turn tight. Some two billion ringgit from a Bank Negara lending maturity is said to leave the market on Thursday.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was stable against the dollar on sufficient liquidity, with short-term swaps easing.
Dealers said there were few market-moving factors and the dollar/rupiah looked trapped within current narrow ranges.
Some selling activity was sighted in short-term swaps early in the session, dampened by ample liquidity.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, supplied some 262 billion rupiah temporarily in the market.
The intervention band was kept at 2,424/2,616 and the conversion band at 2,424/2,472.
Rupiah traded at 2,431.00/2.00 at 0430 GMT, unchanged from opening levels.
Across the Causeway, the Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4267/77 at 0430 GMT, little changed throughout the morning.
Dealers said the outlook was for the currency to stay pinned within the 1.4250/1.4300 range.
The currency was unaffected by the defacto bank Monetary Authority of Singapore's, raising the lending limit to offshore banks to S$200 million from S$150 million on Wednesday.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Jacqueline Wong in Singapore (65-8703199)
